The claim that degree 4 admits non-injective examples conflicts with the Braun–Oréfice-Okamoto degree-4 result, as I recall it. The argument may be right, but I can't check it.
- **Solution 3 (answer 4):** It matches my recollection of Braun–Oréfice-Okamoto (2016) for degree ≤ 4. However, the claim that degree-5 counterexamples exist (attributed to Braun–Fernandes) is unverified, and the sharpness claim is the part that determines the answer. I can't confirm it.

No solution survives falsification at confidence 4 or higher. Each rests on an unverified sharpness claim or an unverified cited result, and the solutions contradict each other on the boundary degree (3, 4, or 5). I have no tools to check the literature, so I can't calibrate any of them above moderate confidence.
